clue.text: Quartz extracted from Abuja's perfect

indicators.note: something extracted is pulled out of a larger source, so the letters lie inside the words Abuja's perfect

explanation.surface: A mining report praising flawless quartz taken from the Nigerian capital, Abuja.
explanation.walkthrough: Abuja is the capital of Nigeria; the apostrophe and space are ignored when reading straight through.
explanation.definitionFit: Jasper is an opaque, often red, variety of microcrystalline quartz used as a gemstone.

clue.text: Apprehension evident in the manner of Royal Marines

parts.note: the French phrase a la means in the manner of

explanation.surface: Fear shows in the way the Royal Marines behave.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm is sudden fear or anxious worry, a state of apprehension.

clue.text: Dance Pablo does badly

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters of Pablo does are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man named Pablo performing a dance poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: The paso doble is a lively Spanish-style ballroom dance modelled on a bullfight.

clue.text: Bird heading away from chicken

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which goes away from the cowardly word

parts.note: chicken is slang for cowardly, craven

explanation.surface: A bird flying off from a hen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicken' seems to be a bird alongside 'Bird', but it means cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: The raven is a large black bird of the crow family.

clue.text: Complaint, one of many that gamekeeper has?

definitions.meaning: a grumble or moan about something

definitions.text: one of many that gamekeeper has?
definitions.meaning: a game bird reared on moorland estates, which a gamekeeper looks after in large numbers

explanation.surface: A grumble about the countryside, perhaps from someone on a shooting estate.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second definition as an example: a gamekeeper tends birds shot for sport.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means a grievance, and it is also the moorland game bird shot on British estates.

clue.text: At sea, no greater supplier of energy

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of no greater are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Out on the ocean, there is no better source of power.
explanation.definitionFit: A generator is a machine that converts mechanical power into electricity, providing electrical power.

clue.text: Due victory, it's secured by own goal

indicators.note: secured means held fast, so the victory word is held inside the own goal letters

parts.note: OG is the football abbreviation for own goal
a victory is a win

explanation.surface: A football team deserved a win, clinched only by the other side's own goal.
explanation.walkthrough: An own goal is when a footballer scores into their own net.
explanation.definitionFit: Money owing is unpaid and payable, so it is due.

clue.text: Detectives order foolish individuals around? That's irregular

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the combined pieces are read backwards

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the British police detectives
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
saps are fools

explanation.surface: Police officers bossing silly people about, which is against the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the detective branch of British police; the Order of Merit is an honour in the gift of the monarch. CIDOMSAPS reads backwards to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Spasmodic means occurring in fits and starts, at irregular intervals.

clue.text: Stuff in food, mostly excellent to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with means coming first, so the excellent word is placed ahead of the food word

parts.note: fab is informal for excellent

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the food word loses its last letter

parts.note: rice is a staple food

explanation.surface: A recipe stuffing a dish with something first-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' looks like a verb about filling food, but it is the noun meaning material.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric is cloth or textile material, which is one sense of stuff.

clue.text: Church will support Irishman's spiritualist meeting

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath, so the church letters come after the Irishman

parts.note: Sean is a typical Irish man's name
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The church backs an Irish man's gathering to contact the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A seance is a session at which a medium tries to contact the spirits of the dead.

clue.text: Gather Jenny maybe is nursing old lady

indicators.note: a nurse holds a patient close, so the donkey word cradles the mother word inside it

parts.note: a jenny is a female donkey, an example of an ass
old lady is slang for one's mother, MA

explanation.surface: Someone called Jenny gathering her elderly relative while caring for her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jenny' looks like a woman's name, but here it is the word for a female donkey, hence the 'maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to collect or accumulate a quantity of things, the same as gathering them.

clue.text: Successfully defend finale to ITV show

indicators.note: a finale is the closing part, so take the final letter of the channel name ITV

parts.note: to show is to indicate or point out

explanation.surface: Someone champions the last episode of a television programme on ITV.
explanation.walkthrough: ITV is a British commercial television channel; 'show' looks like a TV programme but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To vindicate a claim or person is to clear them of blame or justify them, defending them with success.

clue.text: Barking athlete initially managed to maintain fast time

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold or support, so the word for managed holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: managed a business means ran it
barking is British slang for crazy, MAD

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word athlete

explanation.surface: An unhinged sprinter who still kept up a quick time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barking' (short for barking mad) is British slang for insane. 'Fast time' looks like a quick race time but means a period of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramadan is the Islamic month during which Muslims abstain from food and drink in daylight hours.

clue.text: Government of revolutionary African country seizing this writer

indicators.note: to seize is to grab and hold, so the turned country name grips the writer's pronoun inside
something revolutionary turns over, so the country's name is read backwards

parts.note: Niger is a country in West Africa
the setter referring to themself gives ME

explanation.surface: A rebel African government that has taken the author captive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' seems to describe a rebel regime but turns NIGER round to REGIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed system or regime, in the older sense of rule or government.

clue.text: Tirade by star, one officiating at ceremony

parts.note: a star is a celebrity, shortened to celeb
a tirade is a long angry speech, a rant

explanation.surface: A famous person delivering an outburst while conducting a ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrant is the priest or official who leads a religious rite such as a Mass or wedding.

clue.text: Ludicrous rules essentially a huge lab reforms

indicators.note: essentially means at the core, so take the central letter of rules
to reform is to reshape, so the letters of a huge lab are rearranged

explanation.surface: Absurd regulations that mean a huge laboratory must be restructured.
explanation.definitionFit: Laughable means so absurd it deserves ridicule, matching ludicrous.

clue.text: Port, variety going into barrels at intervals

indicators.note: going into means entering, so the variety word is placed inside the alternating letters
at intervals means every other letter of barrels is taken

parts.note: variety, as in the spice of life, is change

explanation.surface: A type of port wine being put into casks one at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' suggests the fortified wine, with barrels to match; it is the Russian Arctic port. Alternate letters of barrels give ARL.
explanation.definitionFit: Archangel (Arkhangelsk) is a seaport in northern Russia on the White Sea.

clue.text: Settle in spot that lacks special ingredient

indicators.note: lacking something means being without it, so these letters are removed from the spot word

parts.note: a splodge is a blot or spot
an ingredient is a component, here the component letters SP that open the word special

explanation.surface: A cook settles for a dish missing its secret component.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Special ingredient' sounds culinary; it means SP, the opening part of the word special, removed from SPLODGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To lodge is to become fixed or settle in a place, as a bullet settles in a wall.

clue.text: Refurbished ancestral royal house

indicators.note: refurbished means done up anew, so the letters of ancestral are reworked

explanation.surface: A family seat, renovated, belonging to the monarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: The House of Lancaster was a branch of the Plantagenets that ruled England in the fifteenth century.

clue.text: Charlie argued regularly with environmentalists' leader, becoming vulgar

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of argued is taken
a leader comes first, so take the opening letter of environmentalists'

explanation.surface: Charlie rowed with the head of a green group and got coarse.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude language or humour is rough and rude, in poor taste, which is what vulgar describes.

clue.text: Stop about third from end of Victoria Line

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the stop word goes round the letter from Victoria

parts.note: to stop is to cease

indicators.note: count back three from the end of Victoria to find the single letter wanted

explanation.surface: Halting near the final stations on London's Victoria Line underground route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victoria Line' looks like the London Underground line; 'Line' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A crease is a fold line pressed into paper or cloth, and also a marked line in cricket.

clue.text: Long-lasting and extremely lucrative account

parts.note: a chronic illness is long-lasting

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters of lucrative

explanation.surface: A durable and highly profitable bank account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Account' looks financial beside 'lucrative' but means a narrative record.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicle is a written record of events in order, a historical account.

clue.text: Tolerate design about to receive investment from university

indicators.note: investment here means being placed within, so the design-and-about string takes the university letter inside

parts.note: a design is an aim or purpose, an end
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Putting up with a plan that is about to get funding from a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Investment' looks financial but means putting something inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure is to bear or put up with something difficult, to tolerate it.

clue.text: European in Chad mistreated mammal

indicators.note: mistreated means badly handled, so the letters of in Chad are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A European visitor in the African country of Chad who abused an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The echidna, or spiny anteater, is an egg-laying monotreme native to Australia and New Guinea.

clue.text: Straighten clothing

definitions.meaning: soldiers line up in a straight row on parade, as when told to form ranks
garments worn, or a woman's one-piece garment

explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers dress ranks to straighten the line, and the word also means clothes or attire.

clue.text: Conservative whip and senior journalist disagreed

parts.note: to whip is to lash
a senior journalist is an editor, abbreviated ED

explanation.surface: A Tory party whip and a newspaper editor had a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip' looks like the parliamentary enforcer beside 'Conservative' but is the verb lash.
explanation.definitionFit: When opinions clash they conflict sharply, so to have clashed is to have disagreed.

clue.text: Tree, one that produces small fruits we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the phrase is spoken, so its sound gives the entry

parts.note: a seeder is something that produces seeds, small fruits

explanation.surface: A tree described by its listeners as one bearing tiny fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech SEEDER and the answer sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: The cedar is a tall evergreen conifer, famous as the cedar of Lebanon.

clue.text: Inn's stolen Ethel's case

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen goods

indicators.note: a case is the outside casing, so take the outer letters of Ethel

explanation.surface: Stolen property is found in Ethel's suitcase at the inn.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel is an establishment offering lodging and meals, like an inn.

clue.text: Recall inadequate qualification male coach concealed

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the whole string of pieces is read backwards
inadequate means falling short, so the qualification word loses its final letter

parts.note: a degree is an academic qualification
a coach is a bus

explanation.surface: A coach with a poor certificate was hidden after being called back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recall' reverses DEGRE + M + BUS, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something submerged is under water and so hidden from view, which makes it concealed.

clue.text: Statutory holiday gets cut for teacher

indicators.note: cutting removes pieces, so the letters of the holiday word are taken out of statutory

parts.note: that the answer also sits forwards inside this word is a coincidence of the deletion: removing the holiday letters leaves the run in place
a stay is a short holiday or visit

explanation.surface: An official public holiday is shortened, perhaps by the education authority.
explanation.walkthrough: S, T, A from the start and Y from the end of STATUTORY spell STAY in order; removing them leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor is a private teacher or one who instructs a small group.

clue.text: Discovered sailors' dining areas aboard very large ship

indicators.note: aboard means on board, so the stripped mess word sits within the very-large pair
discovered here means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters of the messes word come off

parts.note: messes are where sailors eat

explanation.surface: Uncovered naval canteens on a huge ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' reads as found, but here means having the cover (first and last letters) taken off.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel is any craft for travelling on water, a ship or boat.

clue.text: Seldom sees artist going towards bank

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
to bank on is to rely

explanation.surface: A painter is rarely seen walking to the riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks like a riverside or a financial institution, but as a verb it means rely.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarely means not often, on few occasions, which is what seldom says.
